Lab 8 — Prototyping and Design: CampusBike

Chapter 8 lab · kinds of prototypes, dialog map, wireframe review, prototyping risks, from requirements to classes · 10 marks

1. Overview

CampusBike rents bicycles and e-bikes from stations around the campus. A member signs in, sees a map of stations, opens a bike's details, confirms the rental (the e-wallet is charged when the bike is unlocked), rides, and locks the bike at any station to end the rental; the app then shows a return summary. From the map the member can also open My rentals (and the detail of each) and the Profile screen, where they can sign out. If the payment is declined, an error screen lets the member try another card or give up.

A. Prototyping decisions — answer the dimension asked in brackets:

  • S1 — Check whether unlocking a bike over Bluetooth in under 3 seconds is technically possible with the lock vendor’s SDK. (scope?)
  • S2 — Show students what the rental screens could look like at tomorrow’s focus group; quick sketches are enough. (form?)
  • S3 — The prototype will be grown step by step into the real app, with production-quality code from the first day. (future?)
  • S4 — Try three layouts of the map screen in one afternoon and keep only the idea of the best one. (future?)
  • S5 — A clickable Figma prototype of every screen, tested with 8 students on their phones. (form?)
  • S6 — Show the whole flow of screens with fake data and no back end at all. (scope?)

B. Draw the dialog map of the app: one state per screen, one transition per user action (or system result), guards where an action can lead to two screens.

C. Wireframe of the Confirm Rental screen:

+--------------------------------------------+
|  < Back            Confirm rental          |
|--------------------------------------------|
|  Bike #B-117   (e-bike)                    |
|  Station: Library Gate                     |
|  Price: 5,000 VND per 30 minutes           |
|  Pay with: Campus e-wallet  ****2231  [v]  |
|                                            |
|  [ Cancel ]                 [ Confirm ]    |
+--------------------------------------------+
  • FR-21 — The Confirm Rental screen shall show the price per 30 minutes.
  • FR-22 — The Confirm Rental screen shall show the battery level of an e-bike.
  • FR-23 — The Confirm Rental screen shall offer a Cancel action that returns to the Station Map.
  • FR-24 — The Confirm Rental screen shall show the latest time by which the bike must be returned (22:00).
  • FR-25 — The Confirm Rental screen shall show the payment method that will be charged.

D. Statements about prototyping:

  • R1 — Stakeholders who see a polished prototype may push to release it as the product.
  • R2 — A throwaway prototype should include full input validation and defensive coding.
  • R3 — Users may expect the final system to be as fast as a prototype that has no real back end.
  • R4 — A prototype can replace the written requirements once users like it.
  • R5 — Prototype the parts of the system that are uncertain, not the requirements you already understand.
  • R6 — Use plausible data in the prototype so users react to realistic screens.

E. Requirement: "A member unlocks a bike at a station; the system records the start time of the rental, shows the battery level of an e-bike and computes the fee when the bike is returned." Classify W1–W9: W1 member · W2 bike · W3 station · W4 rental · W5 start time · W6 battery level · W7 fee · W8 unlock · W9 compute the fee.

Main features

  • A. Kinds of prototypes.
  • B. The dialog map of the app.
  • C. Wireframe review against the requirements.
  • D. Prototyping risks and success factors.
  • E. From requirements to design candidates.

General requirements

  • In a dialog map, states are screens (a screen may be named with a verb, e.g. "Confirm Rental"); transitions are what the user does.

2. Required project structure

├── a-prototypes.js   ← const PROTOTYPES = { S1: '…', … }
├── b-dialog-map.js   ← const DIALOG_MAP = `stateDiagram-v2 …`
├── c-wireframe.js    ← const WIREFRAME_GAPS = ['FR-…']
├── d-truths.js       ← const PROTOTYPING_TRUTHS = { R1: 'TRUE' | 'FALSE', … }
└── e-design.js       ← const DESIGN_CANDIDATES = { W1: 'CLASS' | 'ATTRIBUTE' | 'OPERATION', … }

4. Functional requirements

1. A. Kinds of prototypes 1.5 marks

Requirements:

  • Scope, future and form of each prototype.

Must use: mock-up proof of concept

Requirements:

  • One start screen, labelled navigations, every screen reachable.

Must use: dialog map

3. B2. Screens and navigation of the case 2.5 marks

Requirements:

  • The screens of the case, the guarded payment result, no dead end.

Must use: navigation

Must use: wireframe

5. D. Prototyping risks 1.5 marks

Must use: throwaway vs evolutionary

6. E. Design candidates 2 marks

Common deductions

  • A dialog map with a screen you cannot leave (Payment Failed with no way back).
  • Two arrows from Confirm Rental on "confirm" with no guard.
  • Treating a liked prototype as the requirements — the SRS is still needed.

7. Submission

Write your answers in the files of answers/ on the right. Diagrams are written as text in the syntax of a real tool (Mermaid or PlantUML — paste them into mermaid.live or plantuml.com to SEE the picture); tables are JavaScript arrays, one object per row of the school template. Press Run for the visible checks and Submit for full grading, hidden checks included. Your mark per question appears in the rubric table.

Lab 8 — Prototyping and Design: CampusBike

Lab chương 8 · loại prototype, dialog map, review wireframe, rủi ro prototyping, từ yêu cầu tới lớp · 10 điểm

1. Tổng quan

CampusBike cho thuê xe đạp và xe điện ở các trạm trong khuôn viên. Hội viên đăng nhập, xem bản đồ trạm, mở chi tiết xe, xác nhận thuê (ví điện tử bị trừ khi mở khoá), đi xe, và khoá xe ở trạm bất kỳ để kết thúc; app hiện tóm tắt lượt trả. Từ bản đồ còn mở được My rentals (và chi tiết từng lượt) và Profile (đăng xuất ở đó). Thanh toán bị từ chối ⇒ màn hình lỗi cho thử thẻ khác hoặc bỏ cuộc.

A. Sáu quyết định prototype S1–S6 — trả lời đúng chiều được hỏi trong ngoặc. B. Vẽ dialog map: mỗi màn hình một trạng thái, mỗi thao tác một chuyển, có guard khi một thao tác dẫn tới hai màn hình. C. Đối chiếu wireframe với FR-21…FR-25. D. Sáu phát biểu về prototyping: đúng/sai. E. Phân loại W1–W9 thành lớp, thuộc tính hay thao tác.

Chức năng chính

  • A. Loại prototype.
  • B. Dialog map của app.
  • C. Review wireframe so với yêu cầu.
  • D. Rủi ro và yếu tố thành công của prototyping.
  • E. Từ yêu cầu tới ứng viên thiết kế.

Yêu cầu chung

  • Trong dialog map, trạng thái là màn hình (tên màn hình có thể là động từ, vd "Confirm Rental"); chuyển là việc người dùng làm.

  • Dialog map có màn hình không thoát được (Payment Failed không có đường về).
